tasks.title: Configuration from the environment: all errors at once
tasks.statement:
Write parse_config(env: &HashMap<String, String>) -> Result<Config, Vec<String>>. Variables: DATABASE_URL (required, must start with «postgres://» or «postgresql://»), PORT (u16, 1–65535, default 8080), LOG_LEVEL (error|warn|info|debug|trace, default info), MAX_CONNECTIONS (1–100, default 10), SESSION_TTL_HOURS (1–720, default 24). ALL errors are collected, in field order, in the format «NAME: reason» (is required / must start with postgres:// / must be a port (1-65535) / must be one of error, warn, info, debug, trace / must be between 1 and 100 (for SESSION_TTL_HOURS it is must be between 1 and 720) / must be a number). An empty string means not set.

Expected output:
```
Ok(Config { port: 8080, database_url: "postgres://u:p@h/db", log_level: "info", max_connections: 10, session_ttl_hours: 24 })
Ok(Config { port: 9000, database_url: "postgresql://u:p@h/db", log_level: "debug", max_connections: 50, session_ttl_hours: 12 })
Err(["DATABASE_URL: is required"])
Err(["DATABASE_URL: must start with postgres://", "PORT: must be a port (1-65535)", "LOG_LEVEL: must be one of error, warn, info, debug, trace", "MAX_CONNECTIONS: must be between 1 and 100", "SESSION_TTL_HOURS: must be a number"])
Err(["PORT: must be a port (1-65535)", "SESSION_TTL_HOURS: must be between 1 and 720"])
```
tasks.hint: For each variable: raw = env.get(..).filter(|s| !s.is_empty()); parse into Result<value, &str>; accumulate a Vec<String>.

tasks.title: Hide the password in a connection string
tasks.statement:
Write redact_url(url: &str) -> String: in a string of the form scheme://user:password@host/path it replaces the password with «***» (if there is no password, the string is unchanged; if there is no «@», it is unchanged). The password may contain «:» and %-sequences; the boundary is the last «@» before the host (the host contains no «@»). The scheme and the user are kept.

Expected output:
```
postgres://app:s3cret@db:5432/chat -> postgres://app:***@db:5432/chat
postgres://app@db/chat -> postgres://app@db/chat
postgres://db/chat -> postgres://db/chat
postgres://app:p:a@ss%40@db/chat -> postgres://app:***@db/chat
postgres://:onlypass@db/x -> postgres://:***@db/x
plain text -> plain text
redis://u:p@h:6379 -> redis://u:***@h:6379
```
tasks.hint: Find «://», then rfind('@') in the remaining part; inside it, the first ':' separates the user.

tasks.title: A Debug that does not reveal the secret
tasks.statement:
The struct DbConfig { host: String, user: String, password: String } must print via {:?} like this: DbConfig { host: "..", user: "..", password: "***" }, with the password hidden. Implement Debug by hand (debug_struct). The wrapper Secret(String) with Debug printing «***» and a method expose(&self) -> &str is the second option: DbConfig2 { password: Secret } with an automatic #[derive(Debug)] also hides the password. Print both and make sure expose returns the real value.

Expected output:
```
DbConfig { host: "db", user: "app", password: "***" }
DbConfig2 { host: "db", password: *** }
s3cret
true
```
tasks.hint: f.debug_struct("DbConfig").field("password", &"***").finish(); for Secret, an impl Debug with write!(f, "***").

tasks.title: A structured log line
tasks.statement:
Write format_log(level: &str, msg: &str, fields: &[(&str, &str)]) -> String: «LEVEL msg k1=v1 k2=v2», with the level in upper case and the fields sorted by key; a value containing a space, an «=» sign or a quote is wrapped in double quotes (inner quotes and backslashes are escaped with a backslash), and an empty value is «""». An empty set of fields means no tail.

Expected output:
```
INFO request
WARN slow ms=250 path=/rooms
ERROR failure empty="" eq="a=b" err="connection refused" id=7 q="say \"hi\""
```
tasks.hint: A function quote(v): quotes are needed if v.is_empty() || v.contains([' ', '=', '"']).

tasks.title: A level filter by target
tasks.statement:
Write Filter::parse(spec: &str) -> Filter and a method enabled(&self, target: &str, level: &str) -> bool. The spec works like RUST_LOG: «info,sqlx=warn,axum::routing=debug»: items separated by commas; an item without «=» is the default level (error if it is not given); «target=level» applies to the target and its submodules (the target matches if target == name or it starts with «name::»). The longest matching rule wins. Levels in increasing verbosity: error < warn < info < debug < trace; a message is allowed if its level is not more verbose than the threshold.

Expected output:
```
chat::rooms info: true
chat::rooms debug: false
sqlx::query info: false
sqlx::query warn: true
axum::routing::router debug: true
axum::serve warn: false
axum::serve error: true
axumx info: true
true false
```
tasks.hint: The order of levels is an array; rules are a Vec<(String, usize)>; choose by the maximum prefix length.

tasks.title: /health and /ready
tasks.statement:
GET /health replies «ok» without touching the database. GET /ready runs SELECT 1 through the pool: success is 200 «ready», an error is 503 «db unavailable». The router is built by the function app(pool). main checks both routes, then closes the pool (pool.close().await) and checks again: /health stays 200, /ready becomes 503.

Expected output:
```
(200, "ok")
(200, "ready")
(200, "ok")
(503, "db unavailable")
```
tasks.hint: State(pool); query_scalar::<_, i32>("SELECT 1").fetch_one(&pool).await.is_ok().

tasks.title: Metrics by path
tasks.statement:
A layer (from_fn_with_state) counts responses by the pair (path, status code) in an Arc<Mutex<BTreeMap<(String, u16), u64>>>. GET /metrics returns text: one line per pair, in key sort order: http_requests_total{path="PATH",code="CODE"} N. The /metrics request itself is not counted (attach the layer only to the other routes with route_layer). Routes: GET /a → 200, GET /b → 404 (StatusCode::NOT_FOUND). main makes several requests and prints /metrics.

Expected output:
```
http_requests_total{path="/a",code="200"} 4
http_requests_total{path="/b",code="404"} 2
http_requests_total{path="/a",code="200"} 4
http_requests_total{path="/b",code="404"} 2
```
tasks.hint: After next.run(req): res.status().as_u16(); the counter is in a BTreeMap; /metrics is a route added after route_layer.

tasks.title: Graceful server shutdown
tasks.statement:
Start axum::serve on port 0 with with_graceful_shutdown: the future completes when a signal arrives on a oneshot channel. The handler GET /slow sleeps for 200 ms and replies «done». The client (raw TCP/HTTP) sends a request; after 50 ms the stop signal is sent; the request MUST complete successfully (200), and then the server task must finish by itself. After that a new connection is impossible (connect fails). Write the function start(shutdown: oneshot::Receiver<()>) -> (SocketAddr, JoinHandle<()>); main is ready.

Expected output:
```
("HTTP/1.1 200 OK", "done")
server stopped: true
new connection: false
```
tasks.hint: axum::serve(listener, app).with_graceful_shutdown(async move { let _ = shutdown.await; }).await.unwrap().

tasks.title: A layer that catches a panic
tasks.statement:
Write a layer with from_fn: it catches a panic in the handler's future (futures::FutureExt::catch_unwind, wrapping the future in AssertUnwindSafe) and, instead of dropping the connection, replies 500 with the body «internal error», recording the reason in a log Arc<Mutex<Vec<String>>> from the state («panic: MESSAGE»). Other requests work as usual. GET /boom panics with the message «boom», GET /ok replies «ok». Check both routes twice.

Expected output:
```
/boom: (500, "internal error")
/ok: (200, "ok")
/boom: (500, "internal error")
/ok: (200, "ok")
(200, "panic: boom;panic: boom")
```
tasks.hint: AssertUnwindSafe(next.run(req)).catch_unwind().await; the message: payload.downcast_ref::<&str>().

tasks.title: Retry with a growing pause
tasks.statement:
Write async fn retry<F, Fut, T, E>(attempts: u32, base_ms: u64, mut op: F, sleep: impl FnMut(u64)) -> Result<T, E>, where op is called again on an error, and between attempts sleep(pause) is called, with the pause doubling: base, 2·base, 4·base… (the last failure does not call sleep). A success is returned immediately. After all attempts have failed, the last error is returned. Check: success on the second attempt, failure of all attempts, success on the first.

Expected output:
```
Ok("success") [100, 200]
Err("failure 3") [50, 100, 200]
Ok(7) []
```
tasks.hint: A loop over attempts; sleep(base << i) between attempts; do not call sleep after the last one.

tasks.title: A circuit breaker
tasks.statement:
Implement Breaker { threshold, cooldown_ms } with states Closed → Open → HalfOpen. allow(now_ms) -> bool: in Closed it is always true; in Open it is false until cooldown_ms has passed since opening; after that it moves to HalfOpen and lets through exactly ONE trial request (true) until that request finishes (a repeated allow in HalfOpen is false). record(ok: bool, now_ms): in Closed, threshold failures in a row open the breaker (the counter is reset by a success); in HalfOpen a success closes it and a failure opens it again (the opening time is now_ms). state(&self) -> &'static str: «closed», «open», «half-open».

Expected output:
```
0: allow=true -> closed
10: allow=true -> closed
20: allow=true -> closed
30: allow=true -> closed
40: allow=true -> closed
50: allow=true -> open
false open
true half-open
false half-open
false open
true half-open
true closed
```
tasks.hint: enum State { Closed, Open(u64), HalfOpen { probing: bool } }; a counter of failures in a row.

tasks.title: The order of a graceful shutdown
tasks.statement:
The Shutdown struct stores the shutdown steps: add(name, step) adds one (a name and a closure returning Result<(), String>). run(&mut self, log: &mut Vec<String>) -> bool runs the steps in the REVERSE of the order they were added (the last one started is stopped first), writes «stop NAME» to the log before a step and «error NAME: REASON» on failure; a failing step does NOT stop the others from shutting down. It returns true if all the steps succeeded. A repeated run does nothing (the steps run once) and returns true.

Expected output:
```
false
["stop accepting connections", "stop websockets", "error websockets: timeout", "stop database"]
true []
true ["stop a"]
```
tasks.hint: Vec<(String, Box<dyn FnOnce() -> Result<(), String>>)>; while let Some(..) = steps.pop().

tasks.title: Migrations: a checksum
tasks.statement:
Write migrate(&PgPool, &[(i32, &str)]) -> Result<Vec<i32>, String>. The service table is _migrations(version INT PRIMARY KEY, checksum TEXT NOT NULL). For each migration in ascending version order: if the version is already applied, compare the stored checksum (the SHA-256 of the SQL text, in hex) with the current one; a mismatch gives Err("applied migration changed N") and a stop; run a new migration together with writing the version and checksum in one transaction (the SQL text goes through sqlx::AssertSqlSafe). Return the versions applied in this call. Check a normal run, a repeat, a changed migration, and adding a new one.

Expected output:
```
Ok([1, 2])
Ok([])
Err("applied migration changed 2")
Ok([3])
applied: 3
```
tasks.hint: sha2::{Digest, Sha256}; hex::encode(Sha256::digest(sql.as_bytes())); sqlx::query(sqlx::AssertSqlSafe(sql.to_string())).

tasks.title: Is a migration safe for zero downtime
tasks.statement:
Write classify(sql: &str) -> Vec<&'static str>, a list of remarks about constructs that are unsafe for a zero-downtime rollout (case-insensitive, collapse whitespace): «drop column» → «dropping a column breaks old code»; «drop table» → «dropping a table»; «rename column» / «rename to» → «renaming breaks old code»; «add column» with «not null» and no «default» → «required column without default value»; «create index» without «concurrently» → «index blocks writes»; «alter column» with «type» → «changing type rewrites the table». An empty list means safe. Remarks come in the order of the rules listed.

Expected output:
```
ALTER TABLE users ADD COLUMN bio TEXT
   []
alter table users add column age int not null
   ["required column without default value"]
ALTER TABLE users ADD COLUMN age INT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0
   []
CREATE INDEX users_name ON users (name)
   ["index blocks writes"]
create   index   concurrently users_name on users (name)
   []
ALTER TABLE users DROP COLUMN bio
   ["dropping a column breaks old code"]
ALTER TABLE users RENAME COLUMN name TO login
   ["renaming breaks old code"]
ALTER TABLE users ALTER COLUMN age TYPE BIGINT
   ["changing type rewrites the table"]
DROP TABLE users
   ["dropping a table"]
ALTER TABLE a RENAME TO b
   ["renaming breaks old code"]
INSERT INTO t VALUES (1)
   []
```
tasks.hint: Lowercase it and collapse whitespace with split_whitespace().join(" "); check with contains.

tasks.title: A separate schema for each test
tasks.statement:
Write the function isolated(&PgPool, name) -> PgPool: it creates the schema t_NAME and returns a NEW pool, every connection of which runs SET search_path TO t_NAME when it connects (PgPoolOptions::after_connect, max_connections(2)). Then two "tests" that create a table with the same name items do not conflict. main runs two such tests in parallel (tokio::spawn); each creates items, inserts its own values and counts the rows; the results and the list of t_* schemas are printed.

Expected output:
```
3 5
["t_alpha", "t_beta"]
```
tasks.hint: after_connect(|conn, _meta| Box::pin(async move { sqlx::query(AssertSqlSafe(format!("SET search_path TO t_{name}"))).execute(conn).await?; Ok(()) })).

tasks.title: A query time limit in the database
tasks.statement:
Write the function slow_query(&PgPool, ms: u64) -> Result<(), &'static str>: it runs SELECT pg_sleep(ms/1000.0) under the limit SET LOCAL statement_timeout = 100 (milliseconds) inside a transaction. If the query was cut off by the timeout (SQLSTATE 57014), return Err("timeout"); any other error is Err("failure"). Call it with 10 ms (success) and with 1000 ms (timeout), and print the results and whether the elapsed time of the second call is under 500 ms.

Expected output:
```
Ok(())
Err("timeout")
fast: true
Ok(())
```
tasks.hint: begin; query("SET LOCAL statement_timeout = 100"); then query("SELECT pg_sleep($1)").bind(f64); the error code is 57014.

tasks.title: Pool exhaustion means 503
tasks.statement:
The application uses a pool of ONE connection with an acquire_timeout of 100 ms (app_with_pool in the starter creates it). GET /slow takes the connection for 400 ms (holds a PoolConnection and sleeps), GET /quick runs SELECT 1. While /slow is running, the /quick request cannot get a connection: the /quick handler must turn the sqlx::Error::PoolTimedOut error into a 503 response with the text «overload» (not 500). After /slow finishes, /quick again replies 200 «ok». Check: /slow and (after 50 ms) /quick in parallel, then /quick after a pause.

Expected output:
```
(503, "overload")
(200, "slow")
(200, "ok")
```
tasks.hint: match sqlx::query_scalar(..).fetch_one(&pool).await { Err(sqlx::Error::PoolTimedOut) => 503, ... }

tasks.title: An end-to-end test over the network
tasks.statement:
The application (the handlers and app(pool) in the starter are ready) is started on port 0. Write http(addr, method, path, token, body) -> (u16, String): a simple HTTP/1.1 client over TcpStream (Connection: close, Content-Length for the body, an Authorization: Bearer header when there is a token), returning the status and the body (everything after the blank line). main walks through a scenario: create a room as anna, write a message, read the history, boris tries to read the history of someone else's room (404), a request without a token (401).

Expected output:
```
(201, "{\"id\":1,\"name\":\"general\"}")
(201, "{\"author\":\"anna\",\"id\":1,\"text\":\"hello over network\"}")
(200, "[{\"id\":1,\"text\":\"hello over network\"}]")
404
401
```
tasks.hint:
Build the request as a string: "{method} {path} HTTP/1.1
Host: x
Connection: close
Content-Length: {n}
..."; read_to_string; split_once("

").

tasks.title: Checking a Dockerfile
tasks.statement:
Write lint_dockerfile(text: &str) -> Vec<&'static str>, remarks in the order of the rules: «no multi-stage build» (fewer than two FROM instructions); «image has no tag or latest» (any FROM instruction whose image name has no «:» or has «:latest»; the alias after AS is not part of the image; --from=... in COPY does not count); «no unprivileged user» (there is no USER, or the last USER is root); «no HEALTHCHECK»; «dependencies are not cached» (there is no COPY Cargo.toml/Cargo.lock before COPY . or COPY src). Instructions are lines that start with a keyword, case-insensitively. An empty text gives all five remarks.

Expected output:
```
[]
["no multi-stage build", "image has no tag or latest", "no unprivileged user", "no HEALTHCHECK", "dependencies are not cached"]
["image has no tag or latest", "no unprivileged user", "no HEALTHCHECK", "dependencies are not cached"]
["no multi-stage build", "image has no tag or latest", "no unprivileged user", "no HEALTHCHECK", "dependencies are not cached"]
```
tasks.hint: Parse the lines: split_whitespace, the first word in upper case; for FROM, the second word.

tasks.title: Priority of configuration sources
tasks.statement:
Write resolve(key: &str, cli: &HashMap<String, String>, env: &HashMap<String, String>, file: &HashMap<String, String>, default: Option<&str>) -> Option<(String, &'static str)>: it returns the value and the source by the priority «cli» > «env» > «file» > «default». An empty value (an empty string) counts as not set and is skipped. The key in env is looked up in upper case with the prefix «CHAT_» (key="port" → CHAT_PORT), in cli and file as is. If it is nowhere, None. Check a table of cases.

Expected output:
```
port: Some(("9000", "cli"))
name: Some(("from-env", "env"))
mode: Some(("prod", "file"))
theme: Some(("dark", "file"))
missing: None
Some(("d", "default"))
```
tasks.hint: A function pick(map, name) -> Option<&String> that filters out empty values.

tasks.title: Idempotent seeding at startup
tasks.statement:
Write seed(&PgPool) -> u64: on every application start it creates the table roles(name TEXT PRIMARY KEY, level INT NOT NULL) (IF NOT EXISTS) and inserts the roles admin (100), moderator (50), member (10) so that a repeated call creates no duplicates and does not overwrite a level changed by hand (ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING). It returns the number of rows actually added. Check: the first call gives 3, a repeat gives 0, after a manual change of a level and another call the value is kept, and after deleting one role the call adds 1.

Expected output:
```
3
0
0
moderator: 75
1
roles: 3
```
tasks.hint: INSERT INTO roles SELECT * FROM UNNEST(..) ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING, or three separate INSERTs with a sum of rows_affected.

tasks.title: Cleaning up old data in batches
tasks.statement:
The table events(id BIGSERIAL, at TIMESTAMPTZ, kind TEXT) contains 25 rows "older than a week" (at = now() − 10 days) and 5 fresh ones. Write purge(&PgPool, older_than_days: i32, batch: i64) -> (u64, u32): it deletes the old rows in BATCHES of batch (DELETE ... WHERE id IN (SELECT id ... WHERE at < now() - interval ... LIMIT batch)) until there is nothing left to delete, and returns (total deleted, number of DELETE queries, including the last empty one). Batches are needed so as not to hold long locks.

Expected output:
```
(25, 4)
[("fresh", 5)]
(0, 1)
```
tasks.hint: A loop: let n = delete(...).rows_affected(); calls += 1; total += n; if n == 0 { break }.

tasks.title: How many connections in the pool
tasks.statement:
Write pool_size(db_max: u32, instances: u32, reserve: u32, cpus: u32, per_cpu: u32) -> u32: the pool size of one instance is min(database connections available per instance, cpus·per_cpu), but not less than 1 (if none are available, it is still 1). The database connections available per instance = (db_max − reserve) / instances (integer division; reserve is kept for administrators and migrations; it must not go negative). Treat instances = 0 as an error: return 0. Check a table of cases.

Expected output:
```
100 4 10 8 4 -> 22
100 1 10 2 4 -> 8
100 10 10 16 4 -> 9
20 4 10 8 4 -> 2
10 4 10 8 4 -> 1
5 4 10 8 4 -> 1
100 0 10 8 4 -> 0
100 3 0 4 2 -> 8
50 5 0 1 1 -> 1
```
tasks.hint: saturating_sub, division, min, max(1).

tasks.title: Aggregate readiness
tasks.statement:
Write readiness(checks: &[(&str, Result<(), &str>)]) -> (u16, String): dependency checks (name, result). If all succeed, (200, «ready»). Otherwise (503, the string «not ready: name1 (reason1), name2 (reason2)» in the order of the checks). An empty list of checks means ready.

Expected output:
```
(200, "ready")
(503, "not ready: db (connection refused)")
(503, "not ready: db (timeout), queue (down)")
(200, "ready")
```
tasks.hint: Collect the failed ones into a Vec<String>, join(", ").

tasks.title: End-to-end test: waiting for an event
tasks.statement:
The server (in the starter) sends the client JSON events in a mix: «typing», «message» with different text, «join». Write a helper function expect_event(c, pred, timeout_ms) -> Result<String, String>: it reads the client's text messages, skipping those for which pred(&str) == false (also skip Ping/Pong), and returns the first matching one; if no matching one arrives within the overall timeout timeout_ms, Err("timeout"); if the connection is closed, Err("closed"). Check searching for a message with text=«needed», searching for a nonexistent event (timeout 300 ms), and closing.

Expected output:
```
Ok("{\"type\":\"message\",\"text\":\"needed\"}")
Err("timeout")
Err("closed")
```
tasks.hint: tokio::time::timeout on the remaining time (deadline = Instant::now() + timeout); a loop: next().await → Text/Ping/Close.

tasks.title: A production set of layers
tasks.statement:
Build app() with routes: GET /ok → «ok», POST /echo (takes the body as a String and returns it), GET /slow (sleeps for 400 ms and replies «slow»). Layers for ALL routes (including 404): a response header x-request-id of the form «req-N» (N is an AtomicU64 counter starting at 1; a layer on from_fn_with_state), a request timeout of 200 ms with status 408 (TimeoutLayer::with_status_code), a body limit of 16 bytes (RequestBodyLimitLayer), permissive CORS. The fallback handler is a 404 with the JSON `{"error":"no such path"}`. Choose the order of layers so that the 408 and 413 responses also get x-request-id. main prints the statuses and headers.

Expected output:
```
200 id=Some("req-1") cors=true
404 id=Some("req-2") cors=true
{"error":"no such path"}
200 id=Some("req-4") cors=true
413 id=Some("req-5") cors=true
408 id=Some("req-6") cors=true
```
tasks.hint: The last .layer added is the outermost layer: x-request-id goes last, so it wraps both the timeout and the limit.

tasks.title: Final application assembly
tasks.hint: Router::new().route(..).fallback(|| async { AppError::NotFound }).method_not_allowed_fallback(h405).with_state(pool).

tasks.title: Your own tracing subscriber
tasks.statement:
Implement Subscriber for Collector (the skeleton with everything else is ready): enabled allows events and spans of level INFO and above (that is, INFO, WARN, ERROR); event collects the fields through Fields (Visit) and adds a line «LEVEL message k=v …» to the shared log (the level as Level::to_string() gives it, fields in the order they are declared in the macro; values as in Debug: strings in quotes, numbers without). new_span returns unique Ids (a counter starting at 1), the other methods are empty. main writes several events of different levels under with_default and prints the collected lines.

Expected output:
```
INFO service started
WARN slow request room=3 user="anna"
ERROR failure code=500
```
tasks.hint: fn event(&self, e: &Event<'_>) { let mut f = Fields::default(); e.record(&mut f); .. e.metadata().level() .. }

tasks.title: Stop signals via select!
tasks.statement:
Write async fn wait_for_stop(interrupt: impl Future<Output = ()>, terminate: impl Future<Output = ()>, deadline_ms: u64) -> Stop: it returns which happened first: «Interrupt» (Ctrl-C), «Terminate» (SIGTERM), or «Deadline» (deadline_ms milliseconds have passed, tokio::time::sleep). If several are ready at the same time, Terminate has priority, then Interrupt (biased; select!). In main, oneshot channels and std::future::pending() are used instead of real signals.

Expected output:
```
Interrupt
Terminate
Terminate
Deadline
true
Interrupt
```
tasks.hint: tokio::select! { biased; _ = terminate => .., _ = interrupt => .., _ = sleep(..) => .. }

tasks.title: A test data builder
tasks.statement:
Write Fixture, a builder for tests: Fixture::new(), .owner(name), .member(name) (can be repeated), .messages(n) for n messages from the owner, and .build(&PgPool) -> FixtureIds { room: i64, users: Vec<i64>, messages: Vec<i64> }. It creates the users (the owner and the members; names are unique), a room named «fixture-ROOM_COUNTER» (the room counter starts at 1 in a static AtomicU32), the members (the owner is also a member), and the messages «m1»…«mN», all in ONE transaction. The tables users, rooms, members, messages are created by main. Check two build calls with shared user names (the second must reuse the existing ones, with no uniqueness errors: ON CONFLICT … RETURNING).

Expected output:
```
FixtureIds { room: 1, users: [1, 2, 3], messages: [1, 2, 3] }
FixtureIds { room: 2, users: [2, 1], messages: [4, 5] }
["fixture-1", "fixture-2"]
members 5, users 3
```
tasks.hint: INSERT INTO users (name) VALUES ($1) ON CONFLICT (name) DO UPDATE SET name = EXCLUDED.name RETURNING id.
